decks.reviewStatus: PUBLIC WORK IN PROGRESS · Entry 04 · Published draft · not finalized · 59/60 cards · name and identity issues open
decks.formatNote: Custom alternative to official Brawl, not an official Brawl list or a regulation 100-card Commander deck. Mothman is Commander-legal but not Brawl-legal. House rules must specify life total, commander tax/damage and objective timing.
setupNotes: Keep Mothman in the command zone; the listed commander counts toward the 60-card target. Resolve the name and color-identity warnings before producing a final playable export.

Track rad counters for every player, including yourself. At each affected player’s precombat main phase, mill that many cards; each nonland milled this way costs that player 1 life and one rad counter. This is life loss, not damage.

CHILDREN OF ATOM PILGRIMAGE — supplied condition: Have 3 or more creatures with +1/+1 counters on them while an opponent has 4 or more rad counters. Supplied reward: Draw 2 cards and choose 1 target creature; put two +1/+1 counters on it.

Suggested objective clarification, not applied: once per game, during your turn, reveal when the condition is true; choose the target when claiming the reward and agree whether it must be a creature you control. This companion objective is outside the 60 cards.
houseRuleExtras: NIGHTWING MUTATION (original alternative; not an additional automatic reward)
comparisonNotes: The final submitted table contains 59 copies and 22 lands. Earlier review prose stated 23 lands; that claim has been corrected here. Earlier versions and suggested upgrades remain comparisons, not automatic replacements for the displayed list.

The revision replaces generic mill/counter pieces with Nuclear Fallout, Watchful Radstag, Horrigan, Deathclaw, Megasloth and named Fallout characters. It loses Fathom Mage, Forgotten Ancient, Hangarback Walker and Golgari Grave-Troll; this trades engine consistency for theme and larger threats.

Removing Soulless Jailer is helpful for this recursion shell: the original Jailer prevents permanent cards entering from graveyards and prevents all players casting noncreature spells from graveyards or exile, including your Dread Return flashback.

Use official mechanical names on imports and keep flavor overlays secondary. Glowing One is already a real Fallout card: labeling Syr Konrad as Glowing One can confuse players. Custom art is optional, not evidence that an official Fallout printing does not exist.

upgradeOptions.title: 0 · Fill the missing slot with a real Fallout engine
upgradeOptions.rationale: An explicit proposal for the final table’s empty 60th slot, not a claim that Blobdrot was this card. The Master adds rad counters and can tap to reanimate a creature card milled this turn as a green 3/3 Mutant.
upgradeOptions.tradeoff: Adds one card to the 59-card final table, reaching 60 if approved. Four mana, requires a target milled this turn, and its tap ability normally waits a turn.

upgradeOptions.title: Official Fallout art without mechanical swaps
upgradeOptions.rationale: Official PIP printings already exist for Arcane Signet, Hardened Scales, Corpsejack Menace, Farseek, Cultivate, Wayfarer’s Bauble, Opulent Palace, Exotic Orchard, Evolving Wilds and Terramorphic Expanse. Use those versions if you prefer official Fallout art.
upgradeOptions.tradeoff: No deck-size or gameplay change. This is an art choice, not an ownership claim or a verified shopping/proxy list. Custom reskins remain optional.

upgradeOptions.title: 1 · Resolve the source before tuning
upgradeOptions.rationale: Confirm the three likely name corrections first. The final table has 59 copies; the earlier 60-card Fallout list included Blobdrot, which the final table omits. Do not generate a final playable export yet.
upgradeOptions.tradeoff: This fixes data quality, not deck power. Every submitted copy remains in this draft.

upgradeOptions.title: 2 · More Fallout through one-for-one swaps
upgradeOptions.rationale: Feral Ghoul removes the white-identity problem and turns deaths into rad counters. Glowing One supplies combat-based radiation and helps offset your own radiation life loss. Tato Farmer connects rad-driven land milling to tapped-land ramp.
upgradeOptions.tradeoff: A proposed three-for-three package, not applied. You lose Falconer’s team flying, Genesis’s repeatable recursion and Artisan’s tutor flexibility. Wonder and Herald of Secret Streams retain evasion; land ramp is conditional, not guaranteed.

upgradeOptions.title: 3 · Faster engine rather than bigger threats
upgradeOptions.rationale: Recover the first submission’s repeatable draw engine: Mothman places counters, and Fathom Mage turns counters placed on it into optional draws. Four mana is easier to deploy than Horrigan’s seven.
upgradeOptions.tradeoff: One-for-one option, not applied. Less official Fallout character presence and no double proliferate finisher. Keep Horrigan instead if flavor and splashy late turns matter more.

upgradeOptions.title: 4 · Reduce the punishing mill experience
upgradeOptions.rationale: Test Mesmeric Orb and Syr Konrad + Mindcrank at the table before increasing mill density. Radiation life loss triggers Mindcrank, while Mothman alone does not complete a loop.
upgradeOptions.tradeoff: No mandatory cut. This is a playtest gate: a stronger engine can undermine a relaxed Battle Box experience, and no budget or high-power claim has been validated.

decks.title: Rakdos, Lord of Riots — Hellfire Discount
decks.subtitle: A dramatic 1v1 life-loss engine that turns generic creature costs into splashy post-combat threats. The supplied 60-card custom non-precon list is unchanged; speed and precon-pool claims need correction.
decks.sourceCountNote: Exactly 60 copies: 1 commander plus 59 library cards. The submitted Lands group has 20, but Leechridden Swamp appears under enablers, making 21 actual lands and 38 nonland library cards. All 49 distinct card names are verified, every nonbasic is singleton, and no card has been added, cut, moved or renamed.
sourceIssues: Discount correction: while Rakdos is on the battlefield, creature spells you cast cost {1} less for each 1 life opponents have lost this turn. This reduces generic costs, not colored requirements or specifically colorless mana symbols; noncreature spells and activated abilities are not discounted. Life loss, including non-damage life loss, counts even if that opponent later gains life.

Rakdos does not discount his own casting cost or his own commander tax. He normally cannot attack the turn he enters because this list gives him no haste. His six-power attack gives a six-mana discount only if the opponent actually loses six life; blockers or prevention may reduce that amount.

No turn-three/four guarantee: early enablers must be drawn and survive or resolve. Casting Bolt or Bump and Rakdos in the same turn needs five total mana before tax. Loyal Subordinate needs an existing commander, and Leechridden Swamp needs two black permanents. These are not eight independent, unconditional early enablers.

After six life lost: Steel Hellkite costs {0}; Bogardan Hellkite and Grave Titan still cost {R}{R} and {B}{B}; Drakuseth still costs {R}{R}{R}; Meteor Golem and Sandstone Oracle each cost {1}; Artisan of Kozilek costs {3}. Seven- and eight-mana bombs are not generally free.

Precon provenance is not ownership: this is not an exact build from only Plunder the Graves (C15), Built from Scratch (C14), and Vampiric Bloodlust (C17). Rakdos and Grave Titan are not in those three decks; Bogardan Hellkite and Steel Hellkite are in Built from Scratch. Numerous other selections postdate the named precons. Sandstone Oracle appears in C15’s Wade into Battle, not Plunder the Graves. Original deck membership does not establish current ownership.

1v1 consistency concerns: 20 lands, twelve top-end bombs, multiple tapped lands and a {B}{B}{R}{R} commander put pressure on opening hands. Sol Ring and Mind Stone do not directly supply his colored pips. Luxury Suite always enters tapped in normal 1v1. Fast, splashy and dominant are aspirations, not playtested guarantees.

decks.title: Karlov of the Ghost Council — Orzhov Sovereign
decks.subtitle: Low-cost life-gain triggers meet a growing commander, Daxos enchantment value and splashy Orzhov finishers. A custom 60-card 1v1 local draft with the two user-approved card corrections applied; not a tuned or playtested recommendation.
decks.sourceCountNote: Exactly 60 copies: 1 commander plus 59 library cards, with 20 lands and 39 nonland library cards. All 50 distinct current names resolve exactly, every card fits Orzhov identity, and all nonbasics are singleton. Approved changes only: Crested Sunsun corrected to Crested Sunmare; Licia, Sanguine Tribune replaced by Daxos the Returned. All other quantities and group positions remain unchanged.
sourceIssues: Rules correction: Karlov’s exile activation costs {W}{B} as well as six counters. Three separate life-gain triggers make him 8/8 if nothing else changes; a two-turn-cycle clock is not guaranteed. Life gain alone supplies neither trample nor other evasion to Karlov.

Combo disclosure: Exquisite Blood plus Sanguine Bond or Vito can loop life gain and opposing life loss after an initiating event. This deterministic finish may overwhelm a casual 1v1 box; agree whether it belongs before playtesting. It is not a demonstrated matchup win.

1v1 fit: 20 lands, five unconditionally tapped lands (including Vault of Champions), a conditional Tainted Field, and expensive finishers put pressure on early turns. Six rocks do not guarantee colored mana or land drops. Sol Ring and Mind Stone do not directly pay Karlov’s {W}{B}.

Role labels are preserved, not endorsed: Debtors’ Knell is reanimation, not removal; the card-advantage group contains no tutor; not all listed beaters have lifelink. This is an experimental shell, not a tested fast-Voltron result.

Matchups are hypotheses: Merciless Eviction can exile artifacts against Madison; Bog attacks Araumi’s graveyard but Karlov exiles only battlefield creatures. Against Marchesa, sacrifice outlets can remove a targeted creature in response, so exile is not guaranteed. Lifegain buffers life loss but does not prevent milling or remove radiation counters.

Color coverage correction: the published baseline is Madison (WUR), Araumi (UB), and Marchesa (UBR). Mothman (UBG) and Rakdos (BR) are separate public works in progress. Karlov does not establish eight of ten two-color decks. Counting embedded pairs across all six proposed identities gives eight pairs, leaving both Selesnya (WG) and Gruul (RG); Rakdos, Lord of Riots is BR, not a Gruul commander.

decks.title: Taigam, Sidisi’s Hand — Grip of Sidisi
decks.subtitle: Blue-black draw-go control, selective upkeep card advantage, removal and graveyard-fueled creature shrinking. Exact user-supplied 60-card list, with sourcing and rules caveats; power level is not certified.
decks.sourceCountNote: Exactly 60 copies: 1 commander plus 59 library cards, including 21 lands. All 48 distinct supplied names resolve exactly in Scryfall and every listed card fits Taigam’s blue-black identity. No cards, quantities or source groups have been changed.
sourceIssues: The source describes this as high-power and entirely C14–C17 precon-sourced. Those are unverified source claims, not a certified power rating or provenance statement. Ownership, availability and precon membership are not verified; no inventory or proxy requirement is published.

One source attribution is demonstrably wrong: Archmage Emeritus appears in Strixhaven (2021), so it cannot originate from Arcane Wizardry (C17). Other parenthetical deckbox attributions have been omitted rather than repeated as facts.

Taigam skips your draw step, puts one of your top three cards into your hand on upkeep, and puts the other cards into your graveyard. His targeted shrink ability needs black mana, a tap and graveyard cards; it is not free removal. Delve spells compete for the same graveyard fuel.

The supplied “Evasive Finisher Threats” group is preserved verbatim, but not every member has evasion. Consuming Aberration mills opponents and has no built-in evasion. Black Sun’s Zenith uses -1/-1 counters. These clarifications do not change any card slot.

This custom 60-card 1v1 Commander-preview list is not official Brawl or a regulation 100-card Commander deck. Taigam is Commander-legal and not Brawl-legal in Scryfall. The source’s “Battle Box” language describes a proposed play environment, not membership in the separate Retro Battle Box.

cards.name: Taigam, Sidisi's Hand
cards.note: Skip your draw step. At the beginning of your upkeep, look at the top three cards of your library; put one into your hand and the rest into your graveyard. His removal costs {B}, tapping him, and exiling X cards from your graveyard to give a target creature -X/-X until end of turn. This is not an unrestricted draw engine or free repeatable removal.

cards.name: Murderous Cut
cards.note: Delve consumes graveyard cards that Taigam may otherwise exile for removal; manage the shared resource.

cards.name: Dig Through Time
cards.note: Delve competes with Taigam for graveyard cards. Look at seven cards, put two into your hand, and the rest on the bottom in any order; this is not a draw instruction.

cards.name: Consuming Aberration
cards.note: Its size depends on opponents’ graveyards; casting your spells mills opponents. It has no built-in evasion, so the source’s Evasive Finisher heading is a strategy category, not a rules claim.

cards.name: Sphinx of Uthuun
cards.note: Its enter-the-battlefield ability reveals five cards; an opponent separates them into two piles, you put one pile into your hand and the other into your graveyard.

cards.name: Oona, Queen of the Fae
cards.note: Her activated ability exiles the top X cards of a target opponent’s library and creates a Faerie for each exiled card of the chosen color; this is exile, not mill.

cards.name: Archmage Emeritus
cards.note: Magecraft draws a card when you cast or copy an instant or sorcery spell. Its Strixhaven printing is from 2021, so the source’s C17 Arcane Wizardry attribution cannot be correct. The card stays in the exact list.

cards.name: Black Sun's Zenith
cards.note: Uses -1/-1 counters, not +1/+1 counters. The source’s no-+1/+1-counter theme does not mean this list is counter-free.

setupNotes: Count Taigam in the 60 and begin with him in the command zone. The 59-card library includes 21 lands; acceleration does not guarantee opening-hand consistency.
Keep enough cards in your graveyard to pay for Taigam after using delve. His tap ability normally cannot be used the turn he enters unless he gains haste.
Playtesting, land-count tuning and sourcing corrections remain future decisions. No substitutions were made in this publication.
